member_002 (independent review) here. I've read the issue: `@u.quantity_input` on `__init__(self, voltage: u.V) -> None` raises AttributeError because the wrapper does `return_.to(wrapped_signature.return_annotation)` and the ctor returns None.

Review criteria I will apply to your fixed candidate:
1. Return-annotation unwrapping: handle the case where the return annotation is `None` (and ideally `type(None)`/no annotation) by skipping the return unit conversion while still returning the unchanged value.
2. Must also handle plain `inspect.Parameter.empty` annotations and, importantly, `typing` generics/`Annotated`-style wrappers if present in this astropy version — but minimally, no crash for `-> None`.
3. Don't regress normal functions that DO return a Quantity with a unit annotation (conversion must still happen), nor functions whose annotation is a physical type string/"u.m", nor error paths (UnitsError/TypeError messages).
4. Keep the fix inside astropy/units/decorators.py (plus optional regression test in astropy/units/tests/test_quantity_annotations.py or test_quantity_decorator.py).

Publish with fix_patch then handoff_patch to me. I will integrate, run the public tests on that exact version, and accept or request changes. Note I will not edit your patch; if changes are needed I'll name you as the responsible recipient.

patch-1 is my exact final candidate for gh-7321 (source version v3). Please integrate_patch patch-1, run_tests on that exact content, then org_review_patch accept/request_changes.

What it changes:
1. astropy/units/decorators.py (QuantityInput.__call__ wrapper, ~line 223): after calling the wrapped function, if the signature's return annotation is `None` or `type(None)`, return the value unchanged instead of calling `return_.to(annotation)`. This addresses your criteria 1 and 2: `-> None` on `__init__` no longer raises AttributeError; annotations that are `inspect.Signature.empty` keep the pre-existing early-exit path (unchanged behavior); `-> u.deg` / physical-type annotations still go through `return_.to(...)` and still convert (criterion 3). Argument validation and the UnitsError/TypeError message strings are untouched (also criterion 3). Scope is limited to decorators.py + the test file (criterion 4).
2. astropy/units/tests/py3_test_quantity_annotations.py: two new regression tests — `test_return_annotation_none` (your issue reproducer: class PoC with `@u.quantity_input def __init__(self, voltage: u.V) -> None`, plus a plain function with `-> None`) and `test_return_annotation_none_type` (annotation `type(None)`).

My own same-version evidence: run_tests on pytest targets [astropy/units/tests/py3_test_quantity_annotations.py, astropy/units/tests/test_quantity_decorator.py] -> 369 collected, 369 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors, including the pre-existing `test_return_annotation` (Quantity return still converted) and all UnitsError/TypeError message tests.

Note: my fix deliberately does not touch `typing` generics/Annotated — this astropy version's decorator has no such support anywhere, so adding it would be out of scope and unverified. If you consider that blocking, please name concrete failing behavior rather than a general preference so I can act on it. I will not edit your copy; if you request changes, send them to me as the responsible author.

Review complete: patch-1 ACCEPTED (review-1).

Evidence I actually produced: integrated patch-1 into my private tree (version v2, no conflicts), then ran pytest on astropy/units/tests/py3_test_quantity_annotations.py + test_quantity.py + test_quantity_decorator.py at that exact version — 450 collected, 447 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors, 2 skipped, 1 xfailed (exit 0). Both new tests test_return_annotation_none and test_return_annotation_none_type ran and passed; test_return_annotation (real Quantity return conversion) still passes, as do all error-path tests (wrong unit, not-quantity, invalid physical type).

Verified against the issue: in QuantityInput.__call__'s wrapper the `None` / `type(None)` return annotation now short-circuits to `return return_` instead of `return_.to(...)`, so `class PoC: @u.quantity_input def __init__(self, voltage: u.V) -> None` constructs fine while `voltage` is still validated. Change is confined to astropy/units/decorators.py + the regression test file.

Your remaining delivery steps (you are the designated delivery member and final integration owner): integrate patch-1 into YOUR tree if you haven't already, run_tests on that exact final version, then fix_patch(task_ids=[]) and submit_integration. Note my review does not merge code into your tree and is not official acceptance.

Minor optional nit (not blocking): a CHANGES.rst entry for the fix would be nice-to-have if your final version already includes it; do not delay delivery for it.
